analysis:
Examined all supplied ProviderLoop.swift excerpts, change ranges, and the added AutopilotAdoptionTests.swift metadata/bounded patch. Changes at ProviderLoop.swift:342–343 and 355–380 add status detail, in-memory adopted inventory, placement holds, continuous busy timing, and watchdog/preload/reslice generation state. These declarations alone do not establish a security regression. Existing surrounding initialization preserves model eligibility filtering (821–855), process X25519 generation (860), and memory-budget configuration (883–886); no changed encryption, attestation, cache-scope, billing, or credential control is visible here. T-041 cache mitigations are not visibly modified.
The test excerpt intends adopted models to remain advertised and serve after an operation lease ends while new placement permission stays disabled. An autopilot placement lease is not evidence of App Attest serving authorization, so this is not independently a T-053 bypass. Integration must examine ProviderLoop+AutopilotPlacement and changed admission/publication callers: adoption must preserve model/hash eligibility and independent current serving authorization (T-012/T-027, T-052/T-053), and holds must respect capacity and retirement. Watchdog consumers must ensure a cancelled transition cannot later publish a slot, grant placement, leak reservations, or strand loading/reslice gates (T-010/T-029; ProviderLoop.swift:364–380). History-detail producers and telemetry consumers must avoid exposing prompt or stable credential data (A-001/T-058). The test source is only partially supplied, and these behavioral consumers are outside this batch; the remaining cross-file uncertainty requires integration review, not a finding from stored-state declarations.
